top_choice_rationale: P002 (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) is a bounded discovery that can be traced to specific papers (Berry 1994; BLP 1995). It solved a concrete identification problem: recovering demand, substitution patterns and markups when prices are endogenous and products are differentiated. About thirty years of use in merger review, regulation, auctions, trade and health give it a track record in practice. Its explicit identifying assumptions can be probed, and the method turns theory into estimates that change practice. The citation should stay anchored in demand estimation and say openly that it does not cover the Bresnahan-Reiss or Benkard-Levin lines. That omission is a real cost of the three-name cap. Pakes' share is probably larger than the other two, so the trio is less symmetric than it looks. Results also depend on functional-form and equilibrium assumptions. I rank P001 (Kiyotaki-Moore pair) a close second. It is a mature, foundational mechanism with the cleanest originator credit, and it was tested in 2007-09. Two things hold it back: the collateral channel is less well identified in direct evidence than BLP's applied record, and the field sits next to the 2022 prize. I treat that adjacency as a modest consideration. I rank P003 (Autor, Dorn, Hanson) third. The China-shock core is credible and has been re-examined repeatedly. But the technology and trade strands blur the unit of recognition, and the work overlaps with the 2021, 2023 and 2024 prizes. All three are credible awards, so I rank no award last. These judgements rest on background knowledge, not verified citation data, and I do not count support as evidence of merit.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile. No documented co-authorship or institutional tie to Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes, Kiyotaki, Moore, Autor, Dorn or Hanson appears in the supplied profile. His principal co-author Steven Kaplan (Chicago Booth) is not credited on any slate proposal. He is an adjunct professor at Chicago Booth and shares SSE affiliation with several committee colleagues. He disclosed these as collegial ties, not adjudicated.
